title: 90-day YouTube practice playbook
portable_start_rule: Day 1 is Monday; move the named weekdays together if your real schedule differs.
rules: Each row is a maximum planned work block, including reading and logging for that task. Record actual minutes.
An upload is conditional on a complete, accurate video with intelligible audio and readable evidence; if blocked, record why and reschedule.
Six long videos are the baseline. Eight are a stretch only after measured capacity supports them.
The baseline uses 8.5 hours per week; at 8 hours reduce scope or cadence, and at 10 hours keep the remaining 1.5 hours as buffer before selling it.
Paid delivery, outreach, tool learning, and optional Shorts must fit the same time budget or replace other work.
The plan promises neither views nor subscribers nor $10,000 by day 90. The revenue scenario is a later mature-business model.
These are learner actions for future use; generating this schedule did not publish, send, purchase, create accounts, or deploy anything.

days.action: Write the first channel brief
days.done_condition: Name one viewer, one recurring problem, three useful pillars, three original premises, and the 8–10-hour weekly limit.

days.action: Collect ten real questions for the pilot
days.done_condition: Save ten paraphrased public or appropriately permitted questions with source links; mark repeated tasks without inventing demand.

days.action: Record a thirty-second screen-and-voice test
days.done_condition: Play the clip on headphones and ordinary speakers; note one sound issue and one readability issue to fix.

days.action: Complete the smallest editing exercise
days.done_condition: Import the test, remove one pause, add one readable label, adjust speech level, and export a playable file.

days.action: Choose and constrain the first promise
days.done_condition: Keep one premise, one visible result, one central explanation, and a draft title; park every extra feature.

days.action: Build the pilot's tiny synthetic demonstration
days.done_condition: Make a bookmark-to-study example show one controlled failure and one improvement using material you own.

days.action: Outline video 1 and test the promise
days.done_condition: Create the hook-to-result outline; obtain an intended viewer reaction if available, or record that outside feedback is missing.

days.action: Write video 1 as spoken sections
days.done_condition: Finish short narration blocks and a shot list; read the opening aloud and replace essay-like wording.

days.action: Capture video 1's clean screen evidence
days.done_condition: Record the result, failure, fix, and retest in separate usable clips; remove confidential information from the scene.

days.action: Record video 1's narration and brief introduction
days.done_condition: Capture the remaining voice sections and optional face-to-camera greeting; listen for clipping and missing explanations.

days.action: Assemble video 1 in teaching order
days.done_condition: Place every essential section on the timeline and remove obvious dead time; the rough cut reaches the promised outcome.

days.action: Repair video 1's most distracting sound or caption issue
days.done_condition: Check speech intelligibility and technical names in key captions; fix the single issue most likely to obstruct understanding.

days.action: Finish video 1's package and export
days.done_condition: Export and watch the whole file; complete a readable thumbnail, accurate description, chapter points if useful, and one next step.

days.action: Release core video 1 if it passes the quality gate
days.done_condition: Publish only after the full review passes; record the URL or the specific blocker, actual cycle hours, and one improvement for video 2.

days.action: Review the first video's promise and reactions
days.done_condition: Record observations separately from interpretations; choose one improvement without treating a tiny sample as a stable average.

days.action: Select an adjacent problem for video 2
days.done_condition: Choose a small test-case or output-checking problem linked to the pilot; show a reproducible example before committing.

days.action: Draft video 2's title and thumbnail as one promise
days.done_condition: Create three title options and one small thumbnail sketch; choose a combination whose promised result the demo can deliver.

days.action: Rehearse video 2's core explanation aloud
days.done_condition: Explain the test cases without reading code line by line; repair the first missing prerequisite you notice.

days.action: Lock video 2's scope against the measured budget
days.done_condition: Compare the first cycle's time with seventeen hours; remove one expensive element if needed and preserve the chosen improvement.

days.action: Finish video 2's script and reusable visual plan
days.done_condition: Write narration and shot cues; create a simple code-label style and caption convention you can reuse.

days.action: Rehearse video 2's difficult segment in the recording scene
days.done_condition: Capture a short sample with the final font and microphone position; verify the planned opening improvement is visible.

days.action: Capture video 2's test-set demonstration
days.done_condition: Record the starting behavior, representative cases, and resulting change; keep the test conditions visible.

days.action: Record video 2's spoken teaching
days.done_condition: Capture narration in small blocks and any brief face-to-camera section; confirm the wording matches the recorded behavior.

days.action: Build video 2's rough assembly with reused styles
days.done_condition: Use the new label convention and remove unnecessary branding; the cut contains the whole explanation.

days.action: Polish video 2's first thirty seconds
days.done_condition: Make the viewer problem and visible result clear early; remove introduction material that delays the promised lesson.

days.action: Check video 2's sound and technical captions
days.done_condition: Listen on an ordinary device and correct the model, variable, and API names used in the explanation.

days.action: Export video 2 and save a clean project template
days.done_condition: Watch the exported file, finish metadata and thumbnail, and save only the reusable elements that reduced confusion.

days.action: Release core video 2 and compare production time
days.done_condition: Publish if ready; record whether the targeted opening improved and whether the two-week scope remained workable.

days.action: Choose the repeated question that deserves a free artifact
days.done_condition: Review the first two videos and available feedback; identify one next task or mark that demand evidence is still sparse.

days.action: Prototype video 3 around that task
days.done_condition: Build the smallest demonstration that makes an output-review or launch checklist useful; avoid adding a second major feature.

days.action: Connect video 3's promise to one checklist
days.done_condition: Write the title, thumbnail concept, and invitation so the video and artifact solve the same specific viewer problem.

days.action: Test video 3's explanation and checklist steps
days.done_condition: Run each proposed check on the synthetic example; remove any instruction whose successful result cannot be observed.

days.action: Cap the free artifact at a usable small scope
days.done_condition: Choose one or two pages or a tiny annotated repository; list the finished example and limitations it must include.

days.action: Draft the free artifact and video 3's spoken outline
days.done_condition: Create the checklist with a completed example, then write the matching narration; use the same terms in both.

days.action: Test resource access and subscription expectations
days.done_condition: Open the file in another profile or device; if using an opt-in, verify clear expectations, delivery, and opt-out in a private test.

days.action: Capture video 3 using the checklist on screen
days.done_condition: Record one check passing and one failure/recovery path; show how a viewer can repeat the check.

days.action: Record video 3's narration and relevant invitation
days.done_condition: Explain the checks and mention the resource after meaningful value; keep only one primary call to action.

days.action: Assemble video 3 with the artifact demonstration
days.done_condition: Place the checklist where it aids the explanation; do not interrupt the core lesson with a prolonged promotion.

days.action: Polish video 3's code and checklist readability
days.done_condition: Inspect the smallest important text on a phone-sized view; enlarge or replace shots that cannot be read.

days.action: Verify video 3's resource link and wording
days.done_condition: Use the intended mobile link route; check that the description says exactly what is provided and what email is requested.

days.action: Finish video 3 and the tested resource edition
days.done_condition: Export and watch the full video; record the resource version, tested download path, and any unsupported setup.

days.action: Release core video 3 with one useful continuation
days.done_condition: Publish if ready; verify the visible resource route after release and record observed visits or the absence of usable evidence.

days.action: Identify a repeatable pattern from the first three videos
days.done_condition: Choose one result-failure-fix structure and one adjacent problem; record why the format could reduce planning work.

days.action: Construct video 4's fair comparison fixture
days.done_condition: Choose two approaches to one task; hold the relevant inputs and scoring rule steady and record limitations.

days.action: Package video 4 around a bounded comparison
days.done_condition: Draft titles that name the task and avoid universal tool rankings; sketch a thumbnail showing the actual tradeoff.

days.action: Retest the comparison and explain the decision
days.done_condition: Run the fixture again where practical, preserve the outputs, and separate the observed result from broader inference.

days.action: Lock the repeat-series format for video 4
days.done_condition: Use the same five-part structure but a materially different engineering problem; reject unrelated news tangents.

days.action: Script video 4 with a visible comparison rubric
days.done_condition: Finish narration, conditions, evidence shots, and limitations; mark one short before-and-after moment that could stand alone.

days.action: Rehearse video 4's evidence sequence
days.done_condition: Confirm that a new viewer can identify each approach, the shared task, and what the scoring result means.

days.action: Capture video 4's comparison evidence
days.done_condition: Record both approaches under the documented conditions; label synthetic fixtures or reconstructions when relevant.

days.action: Record video 4's narration with measured claims
days.done_condition: State what the test showed and did not show; avoid describing one run as proof of a universally best tool.

days.action: Assemble video 4 using the repeat-series structure
days.done_condition: Build the complete comparison with clear transitions; reuse useful styles while keeping substantive teaching distinct.

days.action: Polish video 4's decision and remaining limitation
days.done_condition: Remove repeated setup, clarify the tradeoff, and make the final recommendation conditional on the demonstrated task.

days.action: Check video 4's levels, names, and labels
days.done_condition: Make comparison labels consistent between narration and screen; correct captions and confirm comfortable speech.

days.action: Finish video 4; attempt a derivative Short only within budget
days.done_condition: Allocate up to forty-five minutes to a complete readable vertical moment only if the long-video export is already secure; otherwise skip it.

days.action: Release core video 4 and review series efficiency
days.done_condition: Publish the long video if ready; record whether reuse saved time and keep any Short's results separate from long-video evidence.

days.action: Choose one paid-help hypothesis from real obstacles
days.done_condition: Select notes or a bounded review based on observed questions; if evidence is absent, write the exact question the test must answer.

days.action: Investigate the proposed buyer's existing workaround
days.done_condition: Review permitted responses or public evidence about the task; record what people already try rather than interpreting compliments as purchases.

days.action: Package video 5 as a complete free lesson
days.done_condition: Choose a debugging or review premise whose teaching remains useful without buying; draft one optional continuation.

days.action: Build video 5's diagnostic example and scope boundary
days.done_condition: Demonstrate the review method on your own project; identify what the example can establish and where personal help may differ.

days.action: Estimate the offer's true delivery time
days.done_condition: Count live or writing time, preparation, follow-up, scheduling, and support; remove the offer or reduce other work if it exceeds capacity.

days.action: Create one sample paid deliverable and video 5 script
days.done_condition: Produce a small notes sample or synthetic review report and the narration; specify deliverables, exclusions, and proposed price as a test.

days.action: Check whether the proposed offer is understandable
days.done_condition: Ask an appropriate tester if available or perform a structured desk review; record unanswered fit questions without claiming customer validation.

days.action: Capture video 5's diagnostic walkthrough
days.done_condition: Record the observed problem, investigation, decision, and remaining work; use only material you own or are authorized to show.

days.action: Record video 5's explanation and bounded invitation
days.done_condition: Capture the free method first; mention personal help only with an accurate scope and no promised outcome beyond that scope.

days.action: Assemble video 5 around the learning method
days.done_condition: Keep the worked diagnosis intact and remove sales language that displaces explanation or repeats the invitation.

days.action: Polish video 5's transition from lesson to next step
days.done_condition: Make it clear what the viewer can do independently and what additional support would provide; use one primary continuation.

days.action: Check video 5's sound, captions, and offer references
days.done_condition: Verify that technical terms and any spoken scope agree with the written draft; remove unavailable-product claims.

days.action: Finish video 5 and privately review the offer path
days.done_condition: Watch the export and test the sample/scope access; launch an offer only after the actual terms, fit, and delivery path are ready.

days.action: Release core video 5 and record offer evidence honestly
days.done_condition: Publish if ready; log qualified questions or sales only if they occurred, plus actual delivery commitments and time consumed.

days.action: Choose the strongest improvement for the capstone
days.done_condition: Review five videos, production notes, and repeated questions; select one meaningful change to the recurring small tool.

days.action: Build video 6's final before-and-after fixture
days.done_condition: Make the original failure and improved behavior reproducible on a relevant input; preserve any remaining limitation.

days.action: Package the capstone around its concrete result
days.done_condition: Draft three title options and a thumbnail concept; keep the promise understandable without watching earlier episodes.

days.action: Audit the capstone's evidence and prerequisites
days.done_condition: Check important claims against sources and tests; add the minimum local explanation needed before each essential step.

days.action: Lock capstone scope inside the final two-week cycle
days.done_condition: Cut optional features and visual decoration; reserve time for the complete review and record the single production skill being practiced.

days.action: Finish the capstone script and integrated artifact update
days.done_condition: Write the full narration and shot plan; revise the free checklist only where the new demonstration teaches a real improvement.

days.action: Rehearse the capstone's hardest explanation
days.done_condition: Record a short sample and compare it with day 3's test; correct the most consequential sound or clarity difference.

days.action: Capture the capstone's complete evidence sequence
days.done_condition: Record the starting state, important intermediate steps, final behavior, and one relevant failure boundary.

days.action: Record the capstone's narration and brief personal context
days.done_condition: Explain the reasoning clearly; include only the personal reflection that helps the viewer understand the technical result.

days.action: Assemble the capstone as one complete viewer journey
days.done_condition: Build a coherent cut from promise to result with necessary transitions, labels, and the relevant continuation.

days.action: Polish the capstone for comprehension before decoration
days.done_condition: Inspect the opening, intermediate steps, code size, and ending; remove confusion before adding optional effects.

days.action: Verify the capstone's final sound and captions
days.done_condition: Check speech, technical names, and the artifact version cited; make the final corrections on an ordinary playback device.

days.action: Complete the capstone export and viewer-journey audit
days.done_condition: Watch the entire export and test description links, resource access, thumbnail promise, and any accurately described offer.

days.action: Release core video 6 and record the capstone comparison
days.done_condition: Publish if ready; compare it with the first video using concrete production evidence and record any missed target honestly.

days.action: Audit the six-video library's links and resource delivery
days.done_condition: Test important destinations and files; list factual updates needed and remove broken or misleading next-step routes.

days.action: Review audience evidence at comparable video ages
days.done_condition: Separate traffic sources and formats; record observations, sample limits, and one packaging or retention investigation.

days.action: Reassess the three channel hypotheses
days.done_condition: Compare practical AI engineering, extension engineering, and ML-to-code using viewer fit, your teaching fit, and measured production cost.

days.action: Write the next three video briefs
days.done_condition: For each premise specify the viewer problem, demonstrable proof, central explanation, and next useful step; keep one controlled experiment.

days.action: Reconcile actual hours and real business results
days.done_condition: Record observed revenue, costs, refunds, and commitments only; set unavailable ad or sales revenue to zero and identify the remaining capacity.

days.action: Write the next twelve-week operating decision
days.done_condition: Choose the audience promise, cadence, repeat format, one skill improvement, offer decision, and review date; preserve an achievable weekly budget.
